blurb: In the fragment form of a `context` (the header with no braces), the `exports` clauses come after the `uses` and `consumes` lines and before any `type` or `fn`, so what a unit offers is stated at the top. Move the `exports` line up. `uses` and `consumes` follow the same rule, as `bynk.parse.uses_after_decls` and `bynk.parse.consumes_after_decls`.
example:
context shop.orders
type Id = String
exports transparent { Id }       // ✗ a declaration comes first

context shop.orders
exports transparent { Id }       // ✓ clauses straight after the header
type Id = String
